In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how to improve the semantic video segmentation performance by leveraging information from unlabeled frames, in addition to the labeled ones, in an end-to-end trainable manner?
the development of a weakly-supervised semantic segmentation model that can leverage unlabeled data in order to improve the quality of its temporal predictions, at no additional labeling cost.

the development of weakly supervised video semantic segmentation methods, which is a challenging task, as the amount of labeled video frames that need to be processed in order to train an accurate model is very large.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we propose an end-to-end trainable deep model for semantic video segmentation that is able to leverage the information present in the temporal dimension of the data by means of gated recurrent flow propagation, and that can be trained with only a few labeled frames.

the proposed model can be applied on any semantic segmentation model and improve its performance in the video segmentation task, by leveraging the temporal information from unlabeled frames, at no additional cost.

the model proposed in this paper is capable of improving the performance of static semantic segmentation architectures, by leveraging unlabeled data and temporal information, in an end-to-end trainable manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a weakly supervised, end-to-end trained, video semantic segmentation model that leverages unlabeled frames to boost the accuracy of the segmentation.

we present the first end-to-end trainable model that can temporally propagate semantic information in videos by means of gated recurrent flow propagation, while being able to jointly leverage unlabeled video frames.
our method is able to learn from unlabeled data in a way that improves the performance of a semantic segmentation network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple, end-to-end, weakly supervised video segmentation model can be built by combining a static semantic segmentation architecture with a gated, recurrent flow propagation component.
, by means of gated recurrent flow propagation, it is possible to improve the performance of static semantic segmentation models, by training them to process videos.

the proposed gated recurrent flow propagation module can be used to improve the performance of any static semantic segmentation model, in a plug-and-play fashion, by leveraging temporal information from unlabeled video frames.
